text: Agile methodology is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of doing everything at once, teams work in short phases called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. At the start of each sprint, the team picks tasks from a backlog, which is a prioritized list of all the work to be done. These tasks are often written as user stories, simple descriptions of a feature from the user’s perspective, such as “As a customer, I want to track my order.” Every day, the team holds a quick meeting called a standup, where each member shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any problems they face. This approach supports iterative development, meaning the product is built and improved in small cycles. After each sprint, the team reviews the work and adjusts their plans, allowing them to respond quickly to changes and feedback. This makes Agile flexible and efficient for complex projects.
